You are helping in a project that uses the Taproot design system. Its packages are installed in node_modules.

Build the page as one HTML file named index.html in the current directory, with Taproot's web components. There is no bundler: load what the page needs from node_modules. Write the components as markup in the HTML, not from script. When the file is written, reply with one line saying so.

Build an account settings page. People can change their display name and email address and save the changes, or cancel. Below that, they can delete their account. Deleting asks them to confirm first, because it cannot be undone.

{"results":{"implementation":"web","technology":"web-component","setup":"# Web components setup

What every web component needs, once per project. Each component's own file in this folder maps its
API; `taproot setup --impl web` prints this one.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @taproot-ds/web-components @taproot-ds/tokens
```

## Load the styles

Load the token stylesheet once, at the application root, before any component renders. Without it,
the components have no colors, spacing, or type. The optional base stylesheet styles the page
around them: the base font, text color, background, and a type recipe for each heading level
(`guideline.page-setup`). The components style only themselves.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base"; // optional page defaults
```

Without a bundler, link the files from the tokens package instead:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/base.css" />
```

The components read semantic tokens directly, so they follow the active theme. With no
`data-theme` on the root element, the theme follows the system preference; `data-theme="light"` or
`"dark"` overrides it. The tokens a component reads are not a customization API.

## Fonts

The font tokens name Lora, Source Sans 3, and JetBrains Mono, with system fallbacks. The packages do
not ship the font files. The tokens package's readme has the links to load them.

## Register the elements

Import the package root once to register every element under its `ds-` tag:

```js
import "@taproot-ds/web-components";
```

Or import one component's module and call its define function, as each component's Import section
shows. A define function takes another tag name when `ds-` names collide.

The modules are standard ES modules with no runtime dependencies. Without a bundler, map the bare
package names with an import map, or import the files under `node_modules/@taproot-ds/web-components/src/`.

"}}

Without it, components have no colors, spacing, or type."},{"id":"page-base-text","level":"must","topic":"behavior","statement":"The page's base text uses the body recipe, `semantic.typography.body.md`, in `semantic.color.foreground.default`. Text the components do not draw would otherwise fall back to the platform's default font and color."},{"id":"page-background","level":"must","topic":"behavior","statement":"The page background is `semantic.color.background.default`, so it follows the active theme with the components on it."},{"id":"heading-recipes","level":"should","topic":"behavior","statement":"Each heading level uses a heading recipe: the page title `semantic.typography.heading.lg`, section headings `semantic.typography.heading.md`, subsection headings `semantic.typography.heading.sm`, and deeper levels `semantic.typography.title`. Choose the level by the document outline, and the recipe by the level."},{"id":"base-stylesheet","level":"should","topic":"behavior","statement":"Where the token package offers a base stylesheet for your technology, load it rather than writing the page defaults by hand. It applies these rules with names that are already right. `taproot setup --impl <name>` names it for each implementation."},{"id":"no-guessed-names","level":"must","topic":"behavior","statement":"Take each token's name in your technology from the token package or a lookup, never from a guess. A misspelled token name fails silently and the platform default shows instead."}],"links":{"related":["guideline.compose-or-propose","guideline.accessibility"]},"status":"stable","file":"guidelines/page-setup.md","body":"The components style only themselves. The page around them, the text between them, and the
headings above them get no style from any component. Without these defaults, components look right
while the page around them falls back to the platform's serif font and plain white, and nothing
reports the gap.

## What the page sets

| Page element | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `semantic.color.background.default` | The page itself. Raised areas use `semantic.color.background.surface`. |
| Base text | `semantic.typography.body.md` | Font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. |
| Text color | `semantic.color.foreground.default` | Supporting text uses `semantic.color.foreground.muted`. |
| Small print | `semantic.typography.body.sm` | Captions and fine print. |
| Page title (level 1) | `semantic.typography.heading.lg` | One per page. |
| Section heading (level 2) | `semantic.typography.heading.md` | |
| Subsection heading (level 3) | `semantic.typography.heading.sm` | The recipe Card uses for its title. |
| Deeper headings (levels 4 to 6) | `semantic.typography.title` | The bold sans title Alert and Dialog use. |
| Code | `semantic.typography.code.md` | Inline code and code blocks. |
| Eyebrow above a heading | `semantic.typography.eyebrow` | A short category line, not a heading. |

A typography token such as `semantic.typography.body.md` is a recipe: it groups a font family,
size, weight, line height, and letter spacing, and each is its own token
(`semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily`). Set all five together. Mixing parts of two recipes
produces a size and line height that were never designed together.

For the values in each theme, read the token package, or resolve a component that uses the
recipe, such as `taproot tokens card --part title --resolve`.

## Token names in your technology

A token reference such as `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is technology-neutral. Each
technology's token package publishes it under its own name, and that package says how. In the web
package, a reference becomes a CSS custom property: prefix `--ds-`, join the segments with hyphens,
and turn camel case into hyphenated words, so the reference above is
`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. Check a name against the package's stylesheet
before you rely on it (`no-guessed-names`).

## Fonts

The font tokens name the system's typefaces with fallbacks. The token package does not ship the
font files. Load the typefaces the way your platform does, before the page renders; the token
package's readme lists them and gives the web links to load them. Without them, the fallbacks keep the page readable but it does not
look like the system.

## Theme

The token package follows the reader's light or dark preference, and lets the page choose one
instead. Set the theme at the root of the page so the background, the base text, and every
component change together. A part of the page that sets its own colors without semantic tokens
does not change with them.

## Spacing and layout

Lay out the page with the spacing primitives, `primitives.space.*`, and put product layout
between components rather than inside them (`guideline.compose-or-propose`). The system has no
grid, container, or page template component; compose those in product code.","sections":["what-the-page-sets","token-names-in-your-technology","fonts","theme","spacing-and-layout","load-tokens","page-base-text","page-background","heading-recipes","base-stylesheet","no-guessed-names"]}}

The profile form pairs a secondary "Cancel" action with one primary "Save changes" action. The
primary action completes the routine editing task.

Account deletion is destructive and operates on a different subject. A labeled danger zone
separates it from the profile form. Its supporting text explains the consequence before the person
reaches the destructive Button.

![Account settings action hierarchy](assets/action-hierarchy-settings.svg)

## What this example demonstrates

- Hierarchy applies within an action group rather than across the whole page.
- A supporting action remains visible without competing with the primary path.
- A destructive action is separated from routine actions.
- Button labels name their results.
- Text and structure communicate purpose and risk without relying on color.

## What this example does not decide

The example does not define universal button ordering. Products must follow their established
reading direction and platform convention while preserving the semantic hierarchy.","sections":["what-this-example-demonstrates","what-this-example-does-not-decide","profile-actions","danger-zone","outcome-labels"]}}

| null","description":"The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary."},{"name":"click","kind":"event","event":"activate"}],"parts":{},"items":{},"body":"## Forms

Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set the type when it participates in a form:

```html
<form>
  <!-- form fields -->
  <ds-button type="button" variant="secondary">Cancel</ds-button>
  <ds-button type="submit" variant="primary">Save changes</ds-button>
</form>
```

Use `type="reset"` only when restoring every form control to its initial value is the intended
behavior.

## Styles

Do not recreate Button states with product CSS. Use the published variants and sizes first. Treat
`::part(button)` as an escape hatch that requires a specific product need and design review.

## Icons

Mark a decorative icon hidden from assistive technology. Provide `aria-label` when an icon is the
only visible content.

## Why `aria-label` and not `label`

Button maps `accessibleName` to `aria-label`, while Icon, Spinner, and Tabs map it to `label`. The
difference is deliberate. `aria-label` is the attribute people already put on an icon-only button,
and Button only passes it to the native button inside, so it keeps its standard meaning. The other
three use `label` because their name does more than name: Icon is hidden from assistive technology
without one, Spinner falls back to "Loading", and Tabs names the tab list inside it rather than the
host. They set the name through `ElementInternals` or on that inner element, so the host never
gains `aria-*` attributes. Renaming either side would break published markup.","file":"implementation/button.md"}}}

{"results":{"id":"pattern.action-hierarchy","type":"pattern","title":"Action hierarchy","summary":"Assign action emphasis by importance, support role, and risk, and choose Button or Link by what the control does.","tags":["action","hierarchy","destructive"],"status":"stable","file":"patterns/action-hierarchy.md","body":"Action hierarchy helps a person identify the next action without making every available action
equally prominent.

## Define the action group

An action group contains controls that resolve the same decision or task. A page can contain more
than one action group when the groups act on independent subjects.

Use one `primary` Button for the highest-emphasis action in a group. Do not treat this as a rule that
allows only one primary action on an entire page.

## Assign emphasis

### Primary

Use `primary` for the action that advances or completes the current task. Prefer one primary Button
per action group.

### Secondary

Use `secondary` for a supporting action that should remain visible. It can offer an alternative,
return to the prior state, or dismiss the current task without competing with the primary action.

### Tertiary

Use `tertiary` for a low-emphasis action that remains discoverable in context. Do not use it for the
main path through a task.

### Destructive

Use `destructive` only for a destructive or difficult-to-reverse action. It communicates risk
rather than hierarchy. In a destructive confirmation group, the destructive action can be the
highest-emphasis action and replaces the primary action.

Do not use destructive styling for an error status, warning message, or action that merely needs
more attention. Status colors such as `danger` belong to Alert and Badge, not to actions.

## Choose Button or Link

Choose the control by what happens, not by how prominent it should look. A Button changes
something in the current view or submits a form. A Link takes the person somewhere: another page, a
location on this page, or a file. Do not style a Link as a Button to raise its emphasis, and do not
use a tertiary Button for navigation.

A Link sits beside an action group, not inside its emphasis order. "View billing history" next to
"Save changes" is a Link because it leaves the task without resolving it.

### Inline

Use an `inline` Link inside a sentence. It inherits the surrounding type and stays underlined, so
it does not depend on color to be found.

### Standalone

Use a `standalone` Link on its own line or after the content it relates to, such as "View all
projects" under a list. It uses label type and shows the underline on hover.

## Separate unrelated decisions

Place destructive account or data management actions in their own labeled group. Do not mix a
destructive action into a routine save or cancel group when it operates on a different subject.

## Use clear labels

Name the result of each action. Labels such as "Save changes," "Discard draft," and "Delete account"
make the hierarchy understandable without relying on color.

## Avoid

- More than one primary Button in the same action group
- A primary and a destructive Button competing as terminal actions in one confirmation group
- Destructive styling used only to attract attention
- Tertiary styling for the action required to finish the task
- Disabled actions with no nearby explanation when the reason is unclear
- A Button that only navigates, or a Link that changes data or submits a form
- Relying on control order or color as the only expression of importance or risk","sections":["define-the-action-group","assign-emphasis","primary","secondary","tertiary","destructive","choose-button-or-link","inline","standalone","separate-unrelated-decisions","use-clear-labels","avoid"]}}
